 SCCH.13 3 MVC.8468/2023  JUDGMENT This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Venu Gopalachari S S/o Sudarshana Chari K , in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 27-10-2023 at about 10.00 a.m., deceased Venu Gopalachari S was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA- 40-EB-5302 towards Cheluru circle and when he reached near Cheluru Circle Chintamani, at that time, the driver of the NCRT Container bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AR-5879 (herein after called as alleged offending vehicle) drove the same with very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motorcycle.

As a result,
the accident was caused and thereby Venu Gopalachari S fell down on the road and sustained injuries and died on the spot.
3. The petitioners further have that the accident and death was due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 55 years, working as a Civil Engineer & President of Sri Anantha Vidyasamasthe (proprietary firm) and was earning Rs.80,000/- p.m.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioners No.2 and 3 are children and Petitioner No.4 is father of the deceased and they were depending upon the income of deceased and due to untimely death of deceased, they have suffered mental shock and agony and lost their bread earner of the family.

It is requested to award Rs.50,00,000/- compensation with interest from the Pushpalatha S vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17952960/
2 Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle.
4.

sentences.text: In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their written statement.

5. Respondent No.1 - Insurance company has filed his written statement and denied all the averments of the petition inter alia contending that the owner of the offending vehicle and the police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 159 of MV Act.
The accident was causeD due negligence of driver of offending vehicle and the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL, permit and FC.

The respondent no 1 has disputed with regard to the age, avocation and income of the deceased, relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased and dependency of the Petitioners and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. The Respondent No.2 has filed his separate written statement and admitted that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and the same is insured with the respondent No.1 under the valid and effective policy.
However he denied that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.

He has also disputed with regard to with regard to the age, avocation and income of the deceased, relationship of Petitioners with the deceased and dependency of the Petitioners and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that the death of Venugopalachari S S/o Sudharshanachari K., was only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of NCRT Container bearing No.TN-12-AR-5879 on 27-10-2023, about 10. 00 a.m.,
Cheluru Circle, Chintamani Town, Chikkaballapura District?
2. What compensation petitioners are entitled?
3. What order?
8. In support of their claim, Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.16.
9. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record .

10. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : Partly In the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the final order, for the following:

sentences.text:
ISSUE NO.1:- Petitioners say that on 27-10- 2023 at about 10.00 a.m., deceased Venu Gopalachari S was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-40-EB-5302 towards Cheluru circle and when he reached near Cheluru Circle Chintamani, at that time, the driver of the NCRT Container bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AR-5879 (herein after called as alleged offending vehicle) drove the same with very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motorcycle. As a result, the accident was caused and thereby Venu Gopalachari S fell down on the road and sustained injuries and died on the spot.
12.

In order to substantiate their case, Petitioners have produced FIR, Complaint, requisition to Magistrate, spot mahazar and spot sketch, seizure mahazar, notice, reply, IMV report, Inquest report, PM report and Charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 11.
13.
It is contended by the Respondent - insurance company that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident and it is falsely implicated .
Deceased was not wearing helmet at time of the accident.
Except this suggestion, there are no materials to show that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident.
According to inquest and PM there were lacerated wound run on the chin and multiple fracture of the ribs run on both sides of the chest and the death was due to road traffic accident.
Thus, it is clear that the death was due to the accidental injuries.
14. The Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle after thorough investigation.
The said charge sheet has not been challenged.
All the evidence and materials clearly indicates that it was negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by her.
All the materials show that death of Venu Gopalachari S was due to the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative 15. ISSUE NO.2:-
The Petitioners states that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Venu Gopalachari S.
The Petitioners are the wife, children and father of the deceased.

They have produced the Aadhaar cards of Petitioners, deceased at Ex.P.12 to 16, which clearly indicate that the Petitioner No.1 is wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and Petitioner No.4 is the father of the deceased.

Hence, all the Petitioners are considered as LRs and dependents and they are entitled for compensation.
16.

It is stated that the deceased Venu Gopalachari S was aged 55 years and was working as a Civil Engineer and President of Sri Anantha Vidyasamasthe and was earning Rs.80,000/- p.m. and he was the sole earning member of the family.
To prove the occupation and income, the Petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of proof of income, by considering age of the deceased and date of accident, notional income of Rs.16,000/- per month is taken.
17. The petitioners have not produced any age proof of deceased.

However, on perusal of Ex.P.5 i.e.,
PM report, wherein the age of deceased mentioned as 54 years.
However, Ex.P.12 the Addaar card of the deceased shows that the deceased was born in the year 1967, the same is considered as age of the deceased was 56 years as on the date of accident.
and proper multiplier applicable to the case is 9.
As the age of the deceased is between 50 to 60 years, 10% future prospects is to be added.

As there Pushpalatha S vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17952960/
4 are 4 dependents, 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and the annual income would come to (Rs.13,200 X 12) Rs.1,56,000/- and applying 9 multiplier,
Petitioners are awarded Rs.14,25,600/- towards loss of dependency.

sentences.text: 18. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled Rs.40,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father and Petitioner No.4 has lost his son.

sentences.text: Total Rs.1,60,000/- is awarded towards loss of consortium.
19. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father and Petitioner No.4 has lost his son.
Hence, Rs.15,000/- towards loss to estate.
1 20. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies and other incidental expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award Rs.15,000/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.

21. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency Rs. 14,25,600/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,60,000/-
to Petitioners 3. Loss to estate Rs. 15,000/-
4.

Transportation of Rs. 15,000/-
dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses Total Rs.16,15,600/-
22.
Liability:
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.

With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Pushpalatha S vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17952960/
5 Affirmative.
23.

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.3
: In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .16,15,600/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of amount, 40% of the amount is apportioned to 1st Petitioner, 25%
each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3 and petitioner No.4 is apportioned 10%.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.1, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 2 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.
The entire compensation amount awarded to Petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be disbursed to them through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly over computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 12th day of November 2024).

(Shyla S.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACJM, Member, MACT Court of Small Causes,
Bengaluru.
